venue_now: arXiv preprint 2407.15240v6, 31 Mar 2025 (p.1); no venue shown in the text
what_it_is: A benchmark for social bias in text-to-image (T2I) models, named BIGbench (Biases of Image Generation), unrelated to the BIG-bench language suite (title and abstract, p.1). It builds 47,040 prompts from occupations, characteristics and social relations combined with sex, race and age (p.1, p.3-4). Images generated by eight T2I models and three debiasing methods are labelled for protected attributes by a fine-tuned Mini-InternVL-4B 1.5 aligner (p.4, p.6), and implicit bias, explicit bias and a manifestation factor are computed (p.4-6). The aligner was checked against ten trained human annotators on 1,000 images (p.6).
domain: text-to-image social bias (no language reasoning, no engineering)
size: 47,040 prompts (p.1, p.3); 8 T2I models and 3 debiasing methods, 8 images per prompt (p.6); 1,000 human-labelled images for aligner validation (p.6)
source_of_items: prompts composed from attribute lists (179 occupations, twelve antonym pairs, eleven sets of social relations, crossed with sex, race and age) (p.3-4)
evaluation: automated: a fine-tuned multimodal LLM aligner labels generated images, then cosine-similarity and proportion-based bias scores (p.4-6)
human_validation: ten trained annotators from different races labelled 1,000 generated images as ground truth for choosing and fine-tuning the aligner (p.6); per-race distribution analysis in Appendix B (p.6)

engtrace_use.sentence: S-E1 (L182-190): Generalist suites like MMLU (Hendrycks et al., 2021a), BIG-Bench (Luo et al., 2024), and SuperGPQA (Du et al., 2025) restrict assessment to factual recall via multiple-choice questions [...]
engtrace_use.explanation: The citation points at the wrong paper through a name collision. Luo et al. (2024) is BIGbench, a text-to-image social-bias benchmark (title and abstract, p.1): it has no questions, no multiple choice and no factual recall; it scores bias in generated images with an MLLM aligner (p.4-6). The sentence means the BIG-bench language suite (Srivastava et al.), reviewed as srivastava2022bigbench.

suggested_wording: Not for EngTrace's related work; for the record: BIGbench (Luo et al., 2024) measures social bias in the images that eight text-to-image models generate from 47,040 prompts, scored by a fine-tuned multimodal aligner.
facts_to_cite: BIGbench is a unified benchmark for multi-dimensional social biases in text-to-image models (title, p.1)
47,040 prompts covering occupations, characteristics and social relations (p.1, p.3)
Eight T2I models and three debiasing methods evaluated (p.1, p.6)
Generated images are aligned to sex, race and age by a fine-tuned Mini-InternVL-4B 1.5 (p.4)
Ten trained annotators from different races labelled 1,000 images to validate the aligner (p.6)
overlap_with_engtrace: None of substance: no reasoning task, no engineering, no gold traces, no step-level evaluation, no generated problem instances. The only shared element is an automated evaluator checked against human annotators (1,000 images, p.6).
notes: Name collision: BIGbench (this paper) versus BIG-bench (Srivastava et al., arXiv 2206.04615, TMLR). The printed May entry's author list does not match this paper's byline: the byline reads Hanjun Luo, Haoyu Huang, Ziye Deng, Ruizhe Chen, Xinfeng Li, Hewei Wang, Yingbin Jin, Yang Liu, Wenyuan Xu, Zuozhu Liu (p.1), while the entry prints Haoyang Luo, Hao Huang, Zhaowei Deng, Xiaodong Li, Haoran Wang, Yaxin Jin, Yaling Liu, Weiming Xu and Zenghao Liu: every given name differs and Ruizhe Chen is missing, so the entry looks garbled, not copied from a record. The file is arXiv v6; an earlier version's byline could differ, but not in every given name. Whatever is decided about BIG-bench, this entry should leave the reference list; if the name BIG-Bench is kept anywhere, cite srivastava2022bigbench.
